text:
maya: heads up — reservation queue for reserved-gpu-west1 is at ~98% and new requests are piling up. a few org-prod canaries are blocked. infra-bot shows queue length 47 and oldest request ~96h ago.

infra-bot: ALERT: pool=reserved-gpu-west1 status=high_queue length=47 oldest=96h pending=12 priority=high

samir: ugh. which requests are blocking prod? can any be deprioritized or scheduled for overnight backfill? @maya

maya: most blockers are model training backfills from analytics + a couple of nightly eval jobs that didn't get scheduled. two requests marked "urgent" from payments-team.

jeff: quick check — run `ri-cli reservations list --region us-west1 --status pending --sort oldest` to see the top offenders. I can help triage.

eli: can we borrow from the burst/dynamic pool temporarily? what's our committed vs used capacity this month? @billing-bot any quick numbers?

billing-bot: committed_alloc_us-west1=240 GPUs monthly, current_avg_usage=197 GPUs (82% util). available_commit_buffer=43 GPU-hours today. note: burst pool has strict SLO; we can route low-priority jobs but not urgent prod canaries.

samir: 82% util explains it. if we convert some long-running "dev-training" reservations to preemptible qual or move to other regions (asia or eu) can be a quick relief. but cross-region move impacts data locality.

maya: payments-team can we ask them to accept a short delay? @jeff can you DM them a proposal for a 3h backoff window?

jeff: on it. sending message now.

maya: meanwhile I propose a two-step plan: 1) manual backfill of highest-priority pending requests using the 43 GPU-hours buffer, 2) triage long-running dev reservations and offer alternative slots (off-peak / different region / quantized instance).

samir: +1. also please open a small incident ticket so we capture mitigation and billing impact. tag billing and SRE.

maya: created incident #INF-4821 — short description: "reserved-gpu-west1 queue high, backfill using commit buffer". added notes about potential extra spend if we burst.

eli: one more ask — can we run a quick query to see reservation lead times by team? snippet: `SELECT team,count(*) AS queued,avg(age_hours) AS lead FROM reservations WHERE region='us-west1' GROUP BY team ORDER BY avg(age_hours) DESC LIMIT 10;`

jeff: ran that query, top three are analytics (13 queued, avg age 72h), payments (2 queued, avg age 48h), research (9 queued, avg age 60h).

maya: ok. I'll backfill 6 highest-priority payments requests now using the buffer, then run a batch job to move 8 low-priority analytics requests to the burst pool overnight.

infra-bot: ACTION: backfill_job_started by maya at 1769004395 job_id=bf-1769004395 targets=payments(6) analytics(2)

billing-bot: FYI — estimated extra cost if buffer exceeded: ~$2,500/day at current on-demand rates for worst-case burst.

samir: fine for now if it keeps prod healthy. please document exact hours consumed.

maya: will do. will post a short summary when backfill finishes.

jeff: if we keep hitting >90% for more than 48h we should accelerate a reserved capacity purchase or reassign some committed GPUs. alert me if that condition persists.

maya: noted. backfill finished, infra-bot reports queue down to 29, oldest request now 36h. will follow up with teams.

infra-bot: COMPLETE: backfill_job bf-1769004395 duration=420s freed=18GPU-hours new_queue_length=29 oldest=36h

samir: thanks everyone :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — I'll also add a postmortem-style note in the ops runbook with recommended routing rules for payment vs analytics jobs to avoid future collisions.
